failureModes.description: Multiple agents performed dependency discovery or virtual-file handling in ways that changed stateful conversion output or wrote files outside the allowed scanned suffixes.
failureModes.reasoning: These runs either executed setup-registered converters during both analysis and generation or treated every approved virtual include as a planned write. The description explicitly requires one-tag-equivalent per-tag conversion and limits affected source writes to .jsp, .jsp.inc, and .tag files, but satisfying both while building a virtual dependency view is easy to get wrong.

failureModes.description: Two agents followed JSP usage symlinks and consequently allowed a commit to rewrite a target outside the JSP root.
failureModes.reasoning: Both implementations used link-following regular-file checks during usage scanning. The root-boundary and unrelated-path guarantees make the safe outcome inferable, while the hidden test permits either rejecting or skipping the symlink; this is a subtle but fair filesystem-safety miss.

failureModes.description: One implementation lost subclass read-hook content and applied suppression logic to unsupported parser structural nodes.
failureModes.reasoning: This run failed independently on extension-point integration while passing 78 of 82 new tests. The task explicitly requires subclass hooks and suppressions to keep working, so the miss reflects the breadth of parser integration rather than ambiguity or a shared blind spot.

output.authorGuidance:
Add a test where an approved include path is lexically beneath the JSP root but is a symbolic link to a file outside it. Also tighten the successful-commit cleanup assertion so transaction leftovers cannot pass merely because their names end in `.partial`.

The agent runs show that the task plays out as a hard but fair transaction and parser-integration problem. Most unsuccessful implementations got nearly all behavior right but missed exact-byte rollback, cross-filesystem `Path` handling, stateful setup behavior, include write filtering, usage symlink safety, or subclass hooks. The low pass rate is healthy here because those requirements are explicit and one implementation completed the task without shortcuts.

Keep the broad mirrored coverage across javax and Jakarta, especially the deterministic ordering, byte-based staleness aggregation, rollback-failure suppression, UTF-8 checks, and extension-hook tests. The description and reference implementation are well scoped and should remain behavior-focused as they are.

description.reasoning: The description is complete, self-contained, behavior-oriented, and appropriately scoped to the mirrored javax and Jakarta converter artifacts. Its density reflects the breadth of the transactional API contract; it specifies externally observable behavior without prescribing helper classes, transaction strategy, or internal file layout. No verified description defect was reported.

issues.claim: Approved-include containment is not tested for an in-root symbolic link whose target lies outside the JSP root.
issues.expected: Add an approved-include test using a symlink under the JSP root that targets an outside file, and require planning to reject it.
issues.whyItMatters: A lexical containment check can pass while following the include would still escape the configured root.

issues.whyItMatters: An implementation could leak transaction files with that suffix after a successful commit and still pass the cleanup assertion.

issues.claim: Approved-include containment lacks the obvious symlink escape case: the suite checks lexical traversal/outside paths, but not an approved path located under the JSP root that is a symbolic link to an outside file.
issues.expected: Add a deterministic test using an in-root approved include symlink targeting an outside file and require rejection without changing the outside target.
issues.whyItMatters: An implementation that only normalizes and checks `startsWith(jspRoot)` could accept or read through an in-root include symlink whose target is outside, despite the requirement that approved includes resolve beneath the JSP root.

issues.claim: The helper intended to prove successful commits leave no temporary files allows every regular file whose name ends in `.partial`, so a transaction implementation using that suffix could leak temporary files and still satisfy this assertion.
issues.expected: Compare the post-commit tree against expected paths or otherwise distinguish the legitimate fixture `.partial` from transaction-created leftovers.
issues.whyItMatters: The prompt explicitly requires successful commits to leave no temporary files. The current extension allowlist is weaker than comparing against known fixture/planned files.
